steps.tx: **Microscopic colitis** is an established cause of chronic, watery non-bloody diarrhoea in middle-aged and elderly individuals, predominantly affecting females. It is classified into two primary histological subtypes: **collagenous colitis** and **lymphocytic colitis**. Colonoscopy characteristically reveals endoscopically **normal mucosal appearance** or mild non-specific erythema, emphasizing that definitive diagnosis requires systematic stepped colonoscopic biopsies across both the left and right colon.

rows: Normal or mildly patchy mucosal erythema
Stepped biopsies of right and left colon

steps.tx: The diagnostic histological criterion for **collagenous colitis** is the presence of a continuous thickened **subepithelial collagen band** measuring at least **10** micrometers (**microns**) in depth immediately beneath the surface enterocytes, visualized with Masson trichrome staining. In contrast, **lymphocytic colitis** is diagnosed by an intraepithelial lymphocyte count of at least **20** **intraepithelial lymphocytes** per **100** surface epithelial cells, accompanied by lamina propria chronic mononuclear infiltration.

left.title: Collagenous Colitis Biopsy
points: Masson trichrome stains collagen band blue/green
Subepithelial band >= 10 microns thickness
Surface epithelial sloughing (ragged appearance)
Preserved crypt architecture without architectural distortion

right.title: Lymphocytic Colitis Biopsy
points: Surface enterocyte intraepithelial lymphocytosis
>= 20 IELs per 100 surface epithelial cells
Dense lamina propria plasma cell infiltration
Collagen band remains thin (< 5 microns)

steps.tx: For both collagenous and lymphocytic colitis, oral **budesonide** is the established first-line evidence-based pharmacotherapy for inducing clinical remission. Administered at a dose of **9** mg once daily for an initial course of **8** weeks, budesonide achieves clinical response rates exceeding eighty percent. Its high efficacy and favorable safety profile stem from extensive hepatic first-pass metabolism exceeding ninety percent, which drastically limits systemic corticosteroid bioavailability and side effects.

nodes.label: Histological diagnosis of collagenous or lymphocytic colitis
Oral budesonide 9 mg once daily for 8 weeks
Taper by 3 mg increments every 2 to 4 weeks
Maintenance low-dose budesonide (3 to 6 mg daily) if relapse occurs

steps.tx: A critical step in the clinical evaluation of microscopic colitis is identifying and discontinuing potential culprit medications. Well-established pharmacological triggers include **proton pump inhibitors** (such as lansoprazole and omeprazole), **nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs**, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, and ranitidine. Eliminating these offending drugs can resolve chronic watery diarrhoea and induce histological normalization without requiring prolonged steroid therapy.

steps.tx: Acute and chronic **anal fissures** are painful linear tears in the distal squamous anoderm extending below the **dentate line**. More than ninety percent of primary fissures occur strictly in the **posterior midline**, where the external anal sphincter provides poor muscular support and anoderm microvascular perfusion is poorest. An acute or chronic fissure occurring in an atypical off-midline lateral location must alert the clinician to search for secondary etiologies, including Crohn disease, tuberculosis, syphilis, or HIV.

left.title: Primary Anal Fissure
points: Location: Posterior midline (> 90%) or anterior midline (10%)
Pathophysiology: Hard stool trauma and internal sphincter spasm
Ischaemia: Focal hypoperfusion at posterior midline anoderm
Management: Stool softeners, topical diltiazem/GTN

right.title: Secondary Atypical Fissure
points: Location: Lateral, multiple, or off-midline positions
Pathophysiology: Underlying systemic or infectious pathology
Etiologies: Crohn disease, tuberculosis, anal cancer, HIV
Management: Treat underlying systemic disease

steps.tx: First-line conservative medical therapy for chronic anal fissures aims to relieve internal anal sphincter hypertonicity and restore local anoderm blood flow, termed chemical sphincterotomy. This is achieved using topical vasodilators: **topical diltiazem** **2%** ointment or **topical glyceryl trinitrate** (GTN **0.2%** to **0.4%**) applied to the anal verge twice daily for **6** to **8** weeks. Diltiazem is frequently preferred due to a significantly lower incidence of limiting vascular headaches compared to nitrates.

rows: Apply twice daily for 6 to 8 weeks
Blocks smooth muscle L-type calcium channels
Apply twice daily for 6 to 8 weeks
Nitric oxide donor induces smooth muscle relaxation

steps.tx: For chronic anal fissures refractory to topical chemical sphincterotomy, **lateral internal sphincterotomy** remains the definitive surgical gold standard. By dividing the lower third to half of the hypertrophied internal anal sphincter muscle fibres, LIS permanently reduces resting anal canal pressures and achieves healing rates exceeding ninety-five percent. However, patients must be carefully counseled regarding the permanent risk of minor **flatus incontinence** or liquid stool soiling, which occurs in five to ten percent.

steps.tx: The anatomical trajectory of a cryptoglandular **anal fistula** can be accurately predicted using **Goodsall rule**. A transverse line is drawn bisecting the anal verge. Fistulae with external cutaneous openings located anterior to this transverse line track in a direct radial path straight into the anal canal. Conversely, fistulae with external openings located **posterior** to the transverse line follow a curved, arched trajectory to enter the anal canal at the posterior midline.

left.title: Anterior External Openings
points: Position: Anterior to the transverse bisecting line
Trajectory: Straight radial course into anal canal
Internal opening: Direct radial position at dentate line
Exception: Openings > 3 cm from verge curve to posterior midline

right.title: Posterior External Openings
points: Position: Posterior to the transverse bisecting line
Trajectory: Curved, horseshoe-like arched path
Internal opening: Enters anal canal at the posterior midline
Clinical relevance: Critical for fistulotomy and seton placement
